title: Wire assigned to each port
statement: For a finite Turing machine $M$, natural numbers $n,s,p,h,v$, and a machine case $q$, assign wires to ports as follows. The state port uses the wire for the state in $q$; the input-head port uses the wire for position $p$; and the input-symbol port uses the wire for input cell $p-1$ when $0<p\le n$, otherwise the non-dead summary wire. A work-head port for tape $i$ uses the wire for the encoded head cell of tape $i$ and its head marker; a work-symbol port for tape $i$ and symbol $t$ uses the corresponding symbol wire at that cell. A summary port uses the wire for its Boolean flag, the old-bit port uses wire $v$, and the new-bit port uses wire $v$ shifted by the total width.
caveat: The wire-numbering conventions are expressed using auxiliary offsets and widths whose definitions are embedded in the snippet but have no supplied informal descriptions.
